headline: Revenue surges on AI demand; charge swamps GAAP profit
summary_short: Revenue rose 25% y/y to $16.13 billion, the fastest growth in over fifteen years, and operating income turned positive at $1.80 billion; a $12.5 billion non-cash mark-to-market charge on U.S. government Escrowed Shares drove a GAAP net loss of $11.03 billion ($(2.16) diluted EPS) versus non-GAAP EPS of $0.42.
summary_long: Revenue grew 25% y/y to $16.13B, led by Data Center and AI (+59%) and Intel Foundry (+31%); gross margin expanded 12.9 points to 40.4%. Operating income swung to a $1.80B profit from a $3.18B loss a year ago as restructuring charges fell to $170M from $1.89B and R&D/MG&A spending declined 6%. The $11.03B GAAP net loss was driven almost entirely by a $12.5B non-cash mark-to-market charge on Escrowed Shares tied to the U.S. government's equity stake; non-GAAP net income was $2.20B. Cash and short-term investments fell to $29.7B from $37.4B on $14.3B of partner distributions and debt repayment. Intel guides Q3 revenue to $15.8-16.8B and non-GAAP EPS of $0.38.

drivers.explanation: Growth led by Data Center and AI (+59% y/y) and Intel Foundry (+31% y/y); Client Computing and Physical AI Group rose 13% y/y.
CFO cited volume upside from higher factory yields and improved cycle times as supporting margin gains alongside strong demand.
Swing to profit reflects restructuring and other charges falling to $170M from $1,890M y/y and R&D/MG&A spending down 6%.
GAAP net loss was driven almost entirely by a $12,529M non-cash mark-to-market charge on Escrowed Shares tied to the U.S. government's equity stake.
Diluted EPS loss widened on the same Escrowed Shares mark-to-market charge; non-GAAP EPS excluding it was $0.42.
Cash and short-term investments fell as financing activities used $8.5B, including $14.3B of partner distributions and $9.0B of term-debt repayment.
Debt rose on $13.0B of new term-debt issuance, partially offset by $9.0B of repayments during the quarter.

The q/q equity decline exceeds the quarter's $11.0B net loss alone, consistent with further paid-in-capital and retained-earnings reductions; the release does not narrate the equity movement directly.
CEO cited AI-driven demand and the strongest revenue growth in over fifteen years; CFO cited plans to raise investment in equipment, clean-room space and substrates for expected growth.
